author: GamesIndustry.biz
text:
Funcom to lay off staff as it pivots to focusing solely on Conan Exiles and Dune: Awakening

Norwegian developer Funcom has begun a restructuring process following a decision to focus solely on live operations for Conan Exiles and Dune: Awakening, with an unknown number of staff affected. CEO Rui Casais, who has lead the developer for 11 years including through its 2020 acquisition by Tencent, will leave the business at the end of the year, to be succeeded by Chief Product Officer Scott Junior.

author: GamesIndustry.biz
text:
"I wanted to make the show I wanted to watch" – How Galaxies found a place in the crowded showcase landscape

Tomorrow will see the debut of the fourth Galaxies Showcase, which has managed to carve out a space of its own in the increasingly crowded lineup of digital showcases that have blossomed since the pandemic. Its indie and double-A lineup occupies a careful middle ground between the purely-digital indie collaborations at the bottom of the market and Geoff Keighley's top-dollar showcase at the top – with platform-led events like State of Play and Nintendo Direct occupying rarefied air alongside. Galaxies' pitch is a high-end studio production, anchored by Outside Xbox's Jane Douglas, delivering a tightly curated hour – and no more – of game trailers, mixing paid and free placements.

author: GamesIndustry.biz
text:
Ubisoft closing Trials developer RedLynx and cutting jobs in Singapore studio

Ubisoft has proposed the closure of Finnish studio RedLynx, creator of the Trial franchise, and major job losses at Ubisoft Singapore, lead developer of the ill-fated Skull and Bones. The cuts are the latest in the firm's ongoing restructuring, as it seeks to dramatically reduce costs and reform into a new Creative Houses structure. Both studios had been placed into the Creative Network in that organization, providing central support to other teams.

author: GamesIndustry.biz
text:
Xbox announces Xbox Labs, a new initiative to trial emerging ideas and "new technology"

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced the creation of Xbox Labs, a new team within the organisation to "turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience." The unit is a "a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists," drawn from within the business, charged with rapid development, iteration and testing of tools, products and features that will be judged by the reaction of end users. "We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating," said Sharma in the blog post.
